providerSelection.observed: Acme Identity and Globex Identity were available from the registry sign-in page.

acmeInvitation.observed: An Acme owner created a Reader invitation; the UI showed a copyable invitation link and pending count 1.

acmeAcceptance.observed: The invited Acme user accepted through /organization/accept-invitation and appeared as an active Reader member.

invitationHistory.observed: The Acme owner view showed pending count 0 and Invitation history count 1 with the accepted Reader invitation.

globexInvitation.observed: A Globex owner created a local Globex Research Demo company and a Reader invitation.

globexAcceptance.observed: The invited Globex user accepted and the Company page showed active Owner and Reader members.

readerControls.observed: Reader Company pages showed the Reader role, disabled invitation controls, and owner/admin guidance.

crossCompanyIsolation.observed: Authenticated attempts to set Acme active in the Globex session and Globex active in the Acme session each returned HTTP 403 USER_IS_NOT_A_MEMBER_OF_THE_ORGANIZATION.

organizationEnumeration.observed: The Acme session listed only Acme Candidate Demo and the Globex session listed only Globex Research Demo.

health.observed: GET /health returned ok true, service private-skills, version 0.4.0 after the flows.

limits: The app was built from the historical source snapshot identified above; this evidence does not validate a newer billing or Eve composition.

Provider company metadata exposed Acme Labs, Acme Retail, Globex Research, and Globex Retail, while the local identity database initially contained Acme Candidate Demo; Globex Research Demo was created through the local UI for the second-company flow.
The local issuers are deterministic protocol fixtures and are not production identity providers.
